tools.name: check_prompt
tools.description: Is this user-typed text a prompt injection or jailbreak (an attempt to override, hijack or extract an AI system's instructions)? Returns flagged true/false and a 0-1 score. tools.name: teach_guard
tools.description: Label one prompt for your own guard so it stops repeating a mistake (a false alarm on a normal request, or a missed injection). Needs an API key (get_free_key). About 50 of your own labels cut false alarms from 15% to 4% in our benchmark.

tools.name: get_free_key
tools.description: Create a free Habits account and API key (no email). The key is shown once; set it as the Authorization: Bearer header for this MCP server. The free plan has a fixed $0.10/day spend cap and its own trainable injection guard.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_free_key" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_free_key · Private data: check_prompt, teach_guard, get_free_key · Public sink: get_free_key.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_free_key · Private data: check_prompt, teach_guard, get_free_key · Public sink: get_free_key

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
